Format OTU, taxonomy, and sample data as a phyloseq object

Source: R/vtamR_helper_functions.R
format_for_phyloseq.Rd

Converts OTU/ASV abundance data and taxonomy data into a phyloseq object. Optionally, sample metadata can be included and control samples can be removed.

Usage

format_for_phyloseq(
  otu,
  tax,
  samples = NULL,
  outfile = NULL,
  rm_control = FALSE,
  log_file = NULL,
  sep = ","
)

Arguments

otu

Character string giving the path to the OTU/ASV abundance table, or a data frame. The table must contain asv_id, sample, and read_count columns. Optional columns include asv, replicate, and cluster_id.

tax

Character string giving the path to the taxonomy table, or a data frame. The table must contain an asv_id column and the relevant taxonomic ranks.

samples

Optional character string giving the path to the sample metadata table, or a data frame. When provided, the table must contain sample and sample_type columns. The metadata are added to the resulting phyloseq object as sample data.

outfile

Optional character string specifying the output file path for the phyloseq object. If NULL, the file is not written to disk.

rm_control

Logical; if TRUE, samples whose sample_type is not "real" are removed. When TRUE, samples must be provided.

log_file

Character string specifying the path to the CSV log file. The path is resolved with the following priority:

  1. the log_file argument, if explicitly provided by the user;

  2. the vtamR.log_file option set with options(vtamR.log_file = ...), if set;

  3. "vtamR_log.csv" in the current working directory, used as a last resort if neither of the above is set.

To disable logging entirely, set log_file = NA.

sep

Character used to separate fields in the input files.

Value

A phyloseq object containing:

  • an OTU table with taxa as rows and samples as columns;

  • a taxonomy table containing taxonomy for the taxa present in the OTU table; and

  • sample metadata when samples is provided.

Details

The OTU table is formatted with taxa as rows and samples as columns. If a cluster_id column is present in the OTU table, reads are aggregated by cluster and sample; otherwise, reads are aggregated by ASV and sample. Missing abundances are replaced by zero.

If a replicate column is present, the sample identifier is constructed by combining sample and replicate with a hyphen. The same transformation is applied to the sample metadata when provided.

The taxonomy table contains the columns domain, phylum, class, order, genus, and species. If a kingdom column is present in the input taxonomy table, it is also retained.

Taxa present in the taxonomy table but absent from the OTU table are removed. When sample metadata are provided, only the first metadata row for each sample is retained.

The function requires the phyloseq package. If it is not installed, the function stops and provides installation instructions.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Create a phyloseq object without sample metadata
physeq <- format_for_phyloseq(
  otu = "otu.csv",
  tax = "taxonomy.csv"
)

# Include sample metadata
physeq <- format_for_phyloseq(
  otu = "otu.csv",
  tax = "taxonomy.csv",
  samples = "samples.csv"
)

# Remove control samples
physeq <- format_for_phyloseq(
  otu = "otu.csv",
  tax = "taxonomy.csv",
  samples = "samples.csv",
  rm_control = TRUE
)
} # }
